Fırtına sürerken Birinci Zabit, güvenli: While the storm continues, the Chief Officer monitors the cargo/lashing condition, water ingress and the ship's behavior from safe points (bridge, internal spaces). If slackening lashings, hatch cover leakage or container movement is detected, action is taken only when it is safe and with the Master's approval; any intervention that puts life at risk is avoided.
GMDSS kapsamında EPIRB self-test, SART s: Under GMDSS, the EPIRB self-test, SART self-test, battery and charging checks, DSC test call and radio battery reserve tests are carried out. Depending on the ship's organization, the Safety Officer coordinates these tests with the radio officer or carries them out, and records them in the radio log.
GMDSS teçhizatı; ana güç (ship's main),: GMDSS equipment is supplied from three independent sources: main power (ship's main), emergency power (emergency generator) and the reserve source of energy (battery). The reserve battery must have the capacity to run the GMDSS for a set period (1 hour if the emergency source of electrical power fully complies with SOLAS II-1/42 or 43, including the supply to the radio installations; otherwise 6 hours) when the generator has also stopped.
Gelişmiş ülkeler 2036'ya kadar %85, geli: Developed countries are targeting an 85% reduction by 2036, and developing countries, depending on their group, an 80% reduction by 2045 or an 85% reduction by 2047.
Gemi makine dairesinde kullanılan temasl: Contact temperature sensors used in a ship's engine room (thermocouples, RTDs) work on the basis of this principle.
Gemi çalışanı, vardiya temposu ve fiziks: Because of the watchkeeping routine and the energy demand of physical work, seafarers need a balanced macronutrient intake. The general target is to distribute daily energy so that about 50-55% comes from carbohydrates, 15-20% from protein and 25-30% from lipids. The cook builds this balance in practice by adding to each meal one quality protein (meat, fish, eggs, pulses), one complex carbohydrate (rice, pasta, potatoes, wholegrain bread) and colorful vegetables.
Gemide su, köpük (foam), kuru kimyevi to: Water, foam, dry powder and CO2 portable extinguishers are carried on board; the extinguisher suited to the class of fire (A – solids, B – liquids, C – gases, D – metals, F – cooking oils) is placed at specific stations. Foam + CO2 in the engine room, foam/wet chemical in the galley and water in the accommodation is a typical distribution (CO2 extinguishers are not placed in accommodation spaces). Res. A.951(23) is the guideline for placement and numbers.
Gemiden karaya distress alert iletimi iç: For ship-to-shore distress alerting, at least two separate and independent means are required; the failure of a single device must not remove the distress alerting capability completely. This redundancy principle is the fundamental safety philosophy of GMDSS and explains why the equipment inventory looks "redundant".
Gerekli CII değerleri, 2019 referans değ: The required CII values are tightened by 2 percentage points per year relative to the 2019 reference in 2023-2026 (5% in 2023, 11% in 2026).
Gergin halat koptuğunda depolanan enerji: When a line under tension parts, the stored energy is released and the line recoils (snap-back). According to OCIMF MEG4, snap-back zones painted on deck can give a false sense of security, so the whole mooring area is treated as a potential snap-back zone.
Geri kazanılamayan slop yalnız liman atı: Slops that cannot be recovered are delivered only to a port reception facility. The transfer is recorded in ORB Part II with the appropriate code (Code J, etc.) and the receipt is kept.
Giriş öncesi ve giriş süresince atmosfer: Before and during entry, the atmosphere is measured with a calibrated multi-gas detector for oxygen (for entry it must be at the normal level of air, i.e. about 21% by volume [20.9% on the meter]; lower oxygen can cause loss of consciousness and death without warning), flammable gas (LEL — Lower Explosive Limit; the target is usually below 1% LEL) and toxic gases (H₂S, CO in ppm). Testing is done at different levels (top, middle, bottom) because some gases collect at the bottom and others at the top.
Gravity disc çapı, arıtılacak akışkanın: The gravity disc diameter is selected according to the density of the liquid to be treated. The higher the density, the smaller the disc hole diameter used.
Görev kartı; toplanma yeri (muster stati: The duty card specifies the muster station, the lifeboat/liferaft number, the team role (e.g., fire party, boundary cooling, first aid, communications) and the equipment to be carried. At a crew change, each newly joined AB is given familiarization and a duty card before being assigned shipboard duties; this is a legal requirement.
Gündüz, bir top/küre (ball) demirli, dik: By day, one ball indicates a ship at anchor, two balls in a vertical line NUC, ball-diamond-ball RAM, a cylinder CBD and a diamond a ship engaged in towing. By reading these shapes and lights without hesitation, the officer correctly assesses the Rule 18 priority and the status of the ship. The range of visibility of lights is defined in Rule 22 according to the ship's length.
Güverte stajyeri vardiya zabitinin gözet: The deck cadet takes part in the bridge watch under the supervision of the officer of the watch, but has no authority to make independent decisions. In every situation, the cadet acts only with the OOW's approval. This hierarchy is not accidental: STCW VIII/2 sets out the principle that the officer in charge of the watch "is primarily responsible at all times for the safe navigation of the ship". The cadet cannot share this responsibility, but prepares for it through observation and limited practice.
HMK yapı: α-demir (ferrit), krom, molibd: BCC structure: α-Fe (ferrite), chromium, molybdenum. Can become brittle at low temperature. FCC structure: γ-Fe (austenite), copper, aluminum, nickel. Ductile and easily formed. HCP structure: zinc, magnesium. Limited ductility.
HRU, gemi battığında yaklaşık 1.5–4 m de: The HRU is a pressure-activated device which, when the ship sinks, cuts the lashing securing the liferaft at a depth of about 1.5–4 m by water pressure, allowing the liferaft to float free. Most HRUs (e.g. Hammar H20) are disposable and are replaced every 2 years; the expiry date is printed on them. The Safety Officer records the expiry date of each HRU in the inventory.
HVAC ve soğutma, gemi elektrik yükünün ö: HVAC and refrigeration account for a significant part of the ship's electrical load. The ETO optimizes energy consumption by running compressors and fans on load-following VFD control, by keeping the condenser clean (poor heat transfer increases energy use) and by not keeping set temperatures unnecessarily low. This contributes to the MARPOL Annex VI CII efficiency targets.
Hasarlı conta veya compression bar su gi: A damaged seal or compression bar leads to water ingress; the cargo is wetted by rain/waves (hygroscopic/grain cargoes in particular suffer serious damage).
Hava şişeleri ve kompresörler safety val: Air bottles and compressors are protected by safety valves; a fusible plug releases the air at excessive temperature. If draining is not done regularly, condensed water may lead to corrosion, and accumulated oil to an explosion in the air line. The cadet learns the importance of the draining routine.
Havacılıktaki CRM (Crew Resource Managem: The CRM (Crew Resource Management) concept from aviation was adapted to the maritime sector as BRM. With the STCW 2010 Manila Amendments, ERM was added to the mandatory training syllabus for engineer officers.
Her abandon ship drill'de muster, can ye: Each abandon ship drill includes mustering, correct donning of lifejackets, assembling at the lifeboat/liferaft stations, explaining the embarkation procedure and lowering at least one lifeboat. Lifeboats are launched and maneuvered in the water every 3 months (free-fall lifeboats every 3 months by free-fall or by the secondary means of launching; in addition, a free-fall launch or simulated launching at intervals of not more than 6 months). The rescue boat is launched and maneuvered in the water every month as far as possible, and in any case at least once every 3 months (SOLAS III/19).
Her reefer'ın set-point'i shipper talima: The set-point of each reefer is verified against the shipper's instructions; the control variable is the supply air temperature for chilled cargo and the return air temperature for frozen cargo. A reefer log is kept daily (usually twice a day); alarms are investigated immediately.
Her silindir için exhaust gas temperatur: For each cylinder, the exhaust gas temperature, peak pressure (Pmax) and compression pressure are monitored. The difference in exhaust temperature between cylinders is normally expected to stay within the limit specified by the engine maker. An excessively high cylinder may indicate excess fuel/late combustion, while a low cylinder may indicate an injector fault or a sticking fuel valve.
Hesaplanan EEXI değeri, gerekli EEXI değ: The attained EEXI value must be equal to or below the required EEXI (the reference line value reduced by the reduction factor for the ship type). Otherwise, a technical correction must be made.
IMDG Code paketli tehlikeli yükleri (kon: The IMDG Code regulates packaged dangerous goods (containers, drums, IBCs), while the IMSBC Code regulates solid bulk cargoes (ore, coal). The Chief Officer knows both regimes and applies the correct rules for the type of cargo. Incorrect classification or declaration is among the causes of the most serious marine casualties.
IMO 2020 global sülfür cap'i, gemi yakıt: The IMO 2020 global sulfur cap limits the sulfur content of ship fuel to 0.50% m/m. In ECAs (Baltic, North Sea, North America, the US Caribbean and, from 1 May 2025, the Mediterranean ECA) the limit is much stricter: 0.10% m/m. There are two ways to meet these limits: using compliant low-sulfur fuel, or using high-sulfur fuel with an approved scrubber (EGCS).
ISM (safety) ve ISPS (security) SOLAS'ın: Although ISM (safety) and ISPS (security) derive from different chapters of SOLAS (Chapters IX and XI-2), they should be operated on board as a single integrated management system. The risk assessment methodology, document control, audit logic, corrective action cycle and record-keeping discipline are the same in both. Many companies combine these two systems (sometimes together with MLC and ISO 14001 environmental management) under a single integrated management manual. The Master ensures that these systems work not as separate silos but as a single discipline.
ISM Code'un 10. maddesi, şirketten gemin: Section 10 of the ISM Code requires the company to establish procedures to ensure that the ship and its equipment are maintained in conformity with the relevant rules and regulations and with any additional requirements established by the company. The PMS is the practical application of this section. Within the SMS (Safety Management System), it is defined which equipment is to be maintained, at what interval, with which procedure and by whom.
ISM madde 8, şirketin olası acil durumla: ISM section 8 requires the company to identify potential emergencies (fire, collision, grounding, flooding, pollution, man overboard, abandon ship, security incident, etc.) and to prepare a response plan for each. These plans are on board as the Emergency Response / Contingency Manual and are documents to which the Master has daily access and which the Master knows by heart. Each plan must clearly set out the command structure, roles, communication flow and initial response steps.
Immersion suit (su geçirmez kurtarma elb: An immersion suit delays hypothermia in cold water. It is subject to a seam air pressure test at intervals not exceeding 3 years (more often for suits over 10 years old) and to regular visual inspection; the zipper is waxed with paraffin and the neoprene is checked for cracks. As a rule, SOLAS requires an immersion suit for every person on board cargo ships.
Indicator diagram (PV diyagramı), silind: The indicator diagram (PV diagram) shows how cylinder pressure varies with cylinder volume (piston position) and is the most accurate evidence of combustion quality. Instead of the traditional mechanical indicator, electronic PMI (Pressure Measurement Indicator) systems or permanently fitted cylinder pressure sensors are used today. The Second Engineer takes these measurements at set intervals (generally weekly/fortnightly).
Kamara temizliği \"yukarıdan aşağıya, ku: Cabin cleaning follows the principle "top to bottom, dry work before wet work". First the door is opened for ventilation (respecting the crew member's privacy is essential; personal belongings are not touched). Dusting then starts with high surfaces (tops of lockers, shelves, light fittings), tables and frequently touched surfaces (door handles, switches, telephone) are disinfected, and finally the floor is swept and mopped.
Kamarot servis sırasında nazik, temiz ve: During service, the steward presents a courteous, clean and tidy appearance: clean uniform, apron on and, when necessary, gloves/hairnet. Untidiness raises food hygiene concerns. When coughing/sneezing during service, the steward turns away from the food and hygiene is maintained.
Kapalı alan girişi, ölümlerin en sık yaş: Enclosed space entry is the type of work in which deaths occur most often; a significant proportion of the victims are second persons who go in to rescue. Before entry, O2 (a steady 21% by volume), LEL/flammable gas (target 0%), H2S and CO are measured with a calibrated multi-gas meter. Measurements are taken at different levels of the space (top–middle–bottom) because gases stratify according to their density.
Kapalı mekânlardaki tehlike görünmezdir: The hazard in enclosed spaces is invisible and cannot always be detected by smell: oxygen deficiency, toxic gas (H2S, CO) or an accumulation of flammable gas. In low oxygen, a person can lose consciousness within seconds without any warning. That is why even a tank that "looks fine" can be deadly; entry is made only after testing and with a permit.
Kaptan, Giglio Adası'na yakın \"salute\": The ship ran aground while the Master was making a "salute" maneuver close to Giglio Island. 32 dead. The investigation revealed an unsafe distance off the coast and deficient BRM.
Kaptan, Sea Protest'i not ettirirken (no: When noting the Sea Protest, the Master reserves the right to extend it later; additional evidence is then submitted in an "extended" protest. A Sea Protest does not by itself remove liability; as a formal and timely declaration, however, it places on record the ship's good faith and the facts. The Master applies protest practice under company/P&I guidance.
Karar alındığında: log book'a tam metin: Once the decision is made, it is entered in full in the log book, notified by email to the company's DPA and operations manager, and notified to the charterer. This threefold record is the strongest evidence protecting the Master and the company in any future legal dispute.
Karbon fiyatı dalgalanır; 2024 başı itib: The carbon price fluctuates; as of early 2024 it was in the range of approximately 60-90 €/ton CO₂. This adds 187-280 € per ton to the fuel cost (HFO basis, where 100% of the emissions are covered).
Kargo/balast operasyonları ORB Part II'y: Cargo/ballast operations are entered in ORB Part II in time and completely with the relevant codes. Each completed operation is signed by the officer in charge and each completed page by the Master; the records are kept on board for at least three years.
Kasırga rotasında ısrar, 33 ölü. Ders: e: Persisting on a track into a hurricane; 33 dead. Lesson: the most current weather information and official hurricane advisories must not be ignored; a junior officer's "challenge" must not be suppressed.
Klas, reversible ana makineler için hava: For reversible main engines, class requires the air receivers to provide a certain number (typically 12) of consecutive starts without being recharged. Usually there are two independent compressors and two air receivers; if one fails, the other maintains the starting capability.
Klasik mekanik indicator card (PVT cihaz: The Pmax, Pcomp, Pexp, MIP (Mean Indicated Pressure) and IHP of each cylinder are measured with a conventional mechanical indicator card (PVT device) or a modern electronic PMI (Pressure Measurement Indicator). At least two measurements per voyage (loaded and ballast) are recommended.
Korsanlık/armed robbery riski olan bölge: In areas with a risk of piracy/armed robbery (Gulf of Aden, Gulf of Guinea, approaches to the Singapore Strait, etc.), BMP (Best Management Practices) is applied. Preparation includes registration/reporting with UKMTO and MSCHOA, maximizing speed and freeboard, physical hardening (barbed wire, water curtains, closing off access), enhanced lookout arrangements and preparation of a citadel. Before entering the area, the Master updates the risk assessment and briefs the team.
Krank mili → İtme yatağı (thrust bearing: Crankshaft → Thrust bearing → Intermediate shaft → Propeller shaft → Propeller.
Kullanımda PASS yöntemi uygulanır: Pull: The PASS method is applied in use: Pull (pull the pin), Aim (aim at the base of the flame), Squeeze (squeeze the lever), Sweep (apply with a sweeping motion). The operator must always keep the exit behind them, and the escape route must be kept clear.
Kural 13 (overtaking / geçme), bir gemin: Rule 13 (overtaking) defines a ship coming up with another from a direction more than 22.5 degrees abaft her beam; the overtaking vessel is always obliged to keep out of the way of the vessel being overtaken, and even if the bearing later changes, the situation does not become a crossing and this obligation does not change. Rule 14 (head-on) requires two power-driven vessels meeting on reciprocal or nearly reciprocal courses each to alter course to starboard.
Kural 17, yol hakkı olan (stand-on) gemi: Rule 17 states that the stand-on vessel must keep her course and speed, but that she may take action if the give-way vessel is not taking the required action (Rule 17(a)(ii)), and that she must take action when collision cannot be avoided by the action of the give-way vessel alone (17(b)). In a crossing situation, a power-driven stand-on vessel should, if the circumstances admit, not alter course to port for a vessel on her own port side (17(c)).
Kurutucu ve çamaşır makinesinde biriken: Lint (fabric fluff) that builds up in the dryer and washing machine is a combustible material, and a clogged filter leads to heat build-up and fire. The steward cleans the lint filters after every drying cycle. This simple maintenance removes the most common cause of laundry fires.
Kömür, DRI gibi Group B yükler kendiliği: Group B cargoes such as coal and DRI can self-heat, deplete oxygen and give off hazardous gases (methane/CO from coal, hydrogen from DRI). The Chief Officer implements hold temperature monitoring, oxygen/gas measurement and the ventilation plan. Readings are recorded.
Kütle dengesi: ROB (başlangıç) + alınan: Mass balance: ROB (start) + fuel received − consumption − ROB (end) must equal zero (within tolerance).
Lab raporu gelene kadar yeni alınan yakı: Until the lab report arrives, newly bunkered fuel is not used if possible. If it must be used urgently, the decision is recorded by the Chief Engineer. Laboratories such as FOBAS/VPS give results within 48-72 hours; if the fuel is "off-spec", a Letter of Protest is sent to the supplier immediately.
Laboratuvar raporunda viskozite, su, TBN: The laboratory report gives viscosity, water, TBN, insolubles and wear metals. The trend matters more than a single value; for example, an Fe value that keeps rising from sample to sample is a forewarning of wear that has not yet triggered an alarm. The Oiler catches the change by comparing the results with previous reports.
Lashing zamanla gevşeyebilir (settling,: Lashings can slacken over time (settling, vibration, temperature changes). The Chief Officer plans lashing tightness checks and re-tightening in safe conditions. Before heavy weather the lashings are reassessed and tightened; working on deck once heavy seas have set in is dangerous, so the checks are completed in advance.
Limanda bunker, store alımı, survey ve t: In port, bunkering, storing, surveys and repairs take place at the same time. The Chief Engineer prevents clashes between tasks, assigns a responsible person to each job and keeps safety as the priority. A separate permit and supervision are planned for high-risk work (hot work, enclosed space entry).
MARPOL Annex V, çöpü kategorilere ayırır: MARPOL Annex V divides garbage into categories: plastics (A), food waste (B), domestic waste (C), cooking oil (D), incinerator ash (E), operational waste (F), animal carcasses (G), fishing gear (H), e-waste (I) and cargo residues (J: non-HME, K: HME). The Chief Officer ensures that labeled, color-coded garbage bins are placed at suitable positions on deck and that the crew segregates waste correctly.
MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 18, manifold'da con: MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 18 makes it mandatory to take a continuous drip sample at the manifold (4-way sampler). The sample is divided into 4 bottles: the one retained by the ship (MARPOL bottle, sealed, kept for at least 12 months), the supplier's copy, the one sent to the laboratory and the ship's own commercial sample (ship's sample). The seal number of each bottle is written on the BDN and on the barge's copy; both parties sign.
MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 27 (eski Reg. 22A): Applied since 2019 under MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 27 (formerly Reg. 22A). Ships report their annual fuel consumption, distance traveled and hours spent at sea.
MARPOL bazı atıkların gemide yakılmasını: MARPOL prohibits the incineration of certain wastes on board, such as those containing PCBs, wastes containing heavy metals, refined petroleum products containing halogen compounds and residues of cargoes subject to Annex I, II or III. PVC may be incinerated only in an incinerator with an IMO type approval certificate. General garbage (paper, food waste residues), sludge and waste oil may be incinerated. Incineration is recorded in the Garbage Record Book / Oil Record Book.
MARPOL, bazı denizleri (örn. Akdeniz, Ba: MARPOL regards certain seas (designated "special areas", e.g. the Mediterranean, the Baltic, the North Sea and the Antarctic area) as sensitive, and the waste rules there are much stricter; the distance and conditions for discharging food waste into the sea are tighter, and in some cases delivery ashore is in practice the only option. The cook confirms the rules for the area the ship is in with the responsible officer and plans storage/delivery accordingly.
MLC (Standard A2.3), çalışma ve dinlenme: The MLC (Standard A2.3) provides two alternative limits for hours of work and rest; STCW A-VIII/1 sets only minimum hours of rest. Minimum rest: at least 10 hours of rest in any 24-hour period and at least 77 hours in any 7-day period. Rest may be divided into no more than two periods; one of them must be at least 6 hours long without interruption, and the interval between consecutive rest periods must not exceed 14 hours. Alternatively, the ILO 180 maximum hours of work limit (max. 14 in 24 hours, max. 72 in 7 days) may be applied; the flag State states in the DMLC which one it has chosen.
MLC, denizcilere karadakine eşdeğer, müm: The MLC aims to provide seafarers with medical care comparable to that available ashore, as far as possible free of charge. On board there is a medical chest, a medical guide (the WHO International Medical Guide for Ships or equivalent) and access to medical advice by radio/satellite (TMAS — Telemedical Maritime Assistance Service). Ships carrying 100 or more persons and ordinarily engaged on international voyages of more than 3 days carry a doctor; on other ships, an officer responsible for medical care (usually the Master or the Second Officer, trained in STCW medical care) is assigned.
MLC, denizcilere ücretsiz, yeterli mikta: The MLC guarantees that seafarers are provided, free of charge, with food and drinking water of sufficient quantity and nutritional value that respect cultural/religious diversity. Catering staff (cooks) must be trained and at least 18 years old; on ships with a prescribed manning of 10 or more, a fully qualified ship's cook (certified ship's cook) is required. The Master checks menu variety, adequacy of portions, food stocks, the cold chain and storage hygiene.
MSB genellikle makine kontrol odasında (: The MSB is usually located in the engine control room (ECR). Safe access must be provided at the front and rear.
MSB yangın ve su hasarından korunmalıdır: The MSB must be protected against fire and water damage.
Makine dairesi yüksek gürültü, sıcak yüz: The engine room is an environment with high noise, hot surfaces, rotating equipment and slip hazards. The cadet uses safety shoes, a hard hat, ear protection (mandatory in zones above 85 dB(A)), a boiler suit and, where necessary, eye/face protection. Loose clothing, jewelry and loose hair are a lethal hazard near rotating parts.
Makine dairesinde gürültü seviyesi tipik: The noise level in the engine room is typically between 90 and 110 dB(A). The IMO Noise Code (MSC.337(91); formerly A.468(XII)) sets the noise limits: machinery spaces max 110 dB(A), control room max 75 dB(A).
Merkezi soğutma sistemi (central cooling: On ships with a central cooling system, sea water cooling and fresh water cooling (high/low-temperature circuits) are monitored separately. The temperature difference between the plate cooler inlet and outlet shows the heat transfer efficiency; if the difference is falling, the cooler is clogging or fouling.
Mikro besinler (vitaminler ve mineraller: Micronutrients (vitamins and minerals) are invisible but critical: vitamin C is needed for immunity and tissues, the mineral Fe to prevent anemia, calcium/vitamin D for bones, and B-group vitamins for energy metabolism. The cook ensures this balance by keeping fresh fruit/vegetables, red meat, pulses, dairy products and whole grains on the menu. Variety is the natural guarantee of adequate micronutrient intake.
Modern Alpha lubricator feed rate yöneti: Modern Alpha lubricator feed rate management adjusts the dosage automatically according to engine load and fuel sulfur content. Drain oil analysis (Fe, Sn, Pb, Cu metal trends, BN reserve) is carried out monthly; a rising trend indicates liner/ring/piston wear.
Modern bir tanker veya bulk carrier'in a: The main engine of a modern tanker or bulk carrier is typically a 2-stroke crosshead engine from the MAN B&W ME-C, WinGD X or Wärtsilä RT-flex series. These engines burn HFO (Heavy Fuel Oil), MGO (Marine Gas Oil) or VLSFO (Very Low Sulfur Fuel Oil); LNG dual-fuel and methanol options have become increasingly common since 2020.
Modern dizel makinelerde yataklardaki mi: In modern diesel engines, the minimum oil film thickness in the bearings is in the order of microns; even a 10-20 micron particle can break through the oil film and cause metal-to-metal contact. For this reason, the filter mesh size (e.g. 25-40 microns for ME LO, finer for the injection line) is selected in strict accordance with the manufacturer's specification.
Modern gemilerde HMPE (High Modulus Poly: On modern ships, HMPE (High Modulus Polyethylene — Dyneema/Spectra) lines and mixed polyester/polyamide lines are common. The steel wire + synthetic tail combination is used particularly on tankers. The Chief Officer verifies that the line's MBL is within 100–105% of the SDMBL and that the tail is stronger than the main line (generally 125–130% of the SDMBL).
Modern gemilerde tamamen kapalı (totally: Totally enclosed lifeboats are standard on modern ships; they are watertight, self-righting and motorized. Free-fall lifeboats are released into the sea from a ramp at the stern; they allow rapid abandonment and are common on bulk carriers/tankers. Tankers carrying cargoes with a flashpoint not exceeding 60 °C must carry fire-protected lifeboats.
Modern motorlarda elektronik performans: On modern engines, the electronic performance monitoring system (PMI) provides automatic analysis.
Modern oil monitorlar tamper-proof (kayı: Modern oil monitors are designed to be tamper-proof (logged and sealed); they record when, at what ppm and how much was discharged overboard. This log is cross-checked with the ORB. In special areas (Mediterranean, Baltic, Black Sea etc.), discharge at ≤15 ppm is permitted only while the ship is en route, through an approved OWS with a 15 ppm alarm and automatic stopping; discharging overboard in the Antarctic area and inside ports is prohibited.
NAVTEX (518 kHz) seyir uyarılarını alır;: NAVTEX (518 kHz) receives navigational warnings; the ETO checks the condition of the receiver and antenna. The EPIRB (406 MHz COSPAS-SARSAT) and the SART (Search and Rescue Transponder) require checks of the test function (battery/GPS self-test), the battery expiry date and the hydrostatic release unit (HRU). The EPIRB is tested annually and undergoes maintenance at an approved shore-based facility at intervals not exceeding 5 years; the battery and the HRU are replaced by their expiry dates.
Net yük = (final displacement − light sh: Net cargo = (final displacement − light ship − ballast − fuel − fresh water − constant). All tanks are carefully sounded; the constant must be consistent with previous surveys. A density correction is made.
OMD, ana/yardımcı makine karterindeki ya: The OMD monitors the oil mist density in the crankcase of the main/auxiliary engines. Excessive oil mist is a sign that a bearing/surface is overheating and vaporizing the oil; if this mist reaches its ignition limit, a crankcase explosion occurs. When the mist density rises above the threshold, the OMD triggers a slowdown/shutdown and prevents a major disaster.
Official Log Book (ÖLB), bayrak devletin: The Official Log Book (OLB) is an official book kept in the format of the flag State. Its content varies by flag but typically includes: records of crew joining/leaving, births/deaths, disciplinary incidents, flag Administration instructions, drill records, results of official inspections and important events. Every entry must be dated, timed and signed by the officer concerned/the Master.
Oil Discharge Monitoring and Control Sys: The Oil Discharge Monitoring and Control System (ODMCS) is mandatory on oil tankers of 150 GT and above. It continuously records the discharge rate, oil content, ship's speed and position.
Orifis plakası, boru içine yerleştirilen: An orifice plate is a disk with a hole, fitted in the pipe, which restricts the fluid and creates a pressure difference. This difference is proportional to the square of the flow rate. It is cheap and simple, but it causes a permanent pressure loss.
PSC denetiminde sıkça sorulanlar: ORB do: Questions frequently asked during PSC inspections: is the ORB kept correctly, OWS 15 ppm alarm test, is the sewage system compliant with MARPOL Annex IV, garbage management plan, emergency generator weekly test, bilge alarm test. Vetting (especially on tankers) queries the TMSA elements covering engine room operations and energy management.
PSC denetçisi MLC açısından 16 başlığı k: For the MLC, the PSC inspector checks 16 areas: minimum age, medical certification, qualifications of seafarers, SEA, use of licensed recruitment services, hours of work/rest, manning levels, accommodation, recreational facilities, food/catering, health and safety and accident prevention, on-board medical care, the on-board complaint procedure, payment of wages, financial security for repatriation and financial security for shipowners' liability. If there are "clear grounds" (a seafarer's complaint, a visible violation, an invalid document), a more detailed inspection is carried out.
Pilot/accommodation ladder ve gangway iç: The pilot/accommodation ladder and the gangway are taken in and secured; otherwise they are smashed by the waves and damage the ship's hull. The crane jib is brought to a safe position and secured.
Point of no return (PNR), yakıt/zaman aç: The point of no return (PNR) is the point beyond which turning back is no longer possible in terms of fuel/time; it is critical especially on long ocean passages and in ice navigation.
Pontoon tip: tek parça paneller vinçle k: Pontoon type: single-piece panels are lifted by crane; common on container ships.
Preventive bakım, ekipman üreticisinin ö: Preventive maintenance is carried out at the maintenance intervals recommended by the equipment manufacturer (running hours, calendar period). It covers jobs such as oil changes, filter changes, gasket replacement and adjustment checks.
Product tankerlerde \"compatibility tabl: On product tankers, a "compatibility table" check is made; if there is a previous cargo that could spoil the quality of the oil cargo, a wall-wash test is carried out. For MARPOL Annex II (NLS), the P&A (Procedures and Arrangements) Manual is the guide.
Purifier modunda her desludge sonrası, a: In purifier mode, after each desludge and before separation starts, a set amount of sealing water is fed into the bowl to establish the water seal. This water is the barrier that prevents the fuel from escaping through the water outlet. If the seal is not established properly, fuel escapes through the water outlet (broken seal / oil loss).
RACON, seyir işaretlerine (fener, şamand: A RACON is a transponder fitted on aids to navigation (lights, buoys) that produces a Morse code signal on the radar; observing it is useful for verifying the radar.
Radar arızasında gemiyi 'onarım yaparak': In the event of radar failure, the first duty of the officer of the watch is not to make the ship safe 'by carrying out repairs', but first to make it operationally safe by means of safe speed, an additional lookout, an alternative radar/navigation sensor and, if necessary, a change of course/area.
Radar plotting, hedefin gerçek rotasını: Radar plotting is carried out to determine the target's true course and speed and its CPA (Closest Point of Approach) and TCPA (Time to CPA). In manual plotting, the target's true motion is resolved with the OAW triangle (WO: own ship, OA: relative motion, WA: true motion); ARPA does this automatically, but the officer must question the accuracy of the ARPA data (tracking stability, risk of target swap).
Restricted visibility (Kural 19) özel ol: Restricted visibility (Rule 19) is given particular emphasis; in this situation there is no stand-on/give-way distinction, and every ship makes an early and substantial maneuver based on radar plotting. The Second Officer clearly teaches that in fog an alteration of course to port for a ship forward of the beam (other than a ship being overtaken) and an alteration of course towards a ship abeam or abaft the beam are to be avoided, and that speed must be reduced to a safe level.
Rocket parachute flare, hand flare ve bu: The expiry dates of rocket parachute flares, hand flares and buoyant smoke signals (generally 3–3.5 years from manufacture) are tracked carefully. Expired items are disposed of or handed over properly; the ship does not sail with expired pyrotechnics. They count as visual distress signals under LSA (SOLAS III, LSA Code).
Rüzgâr ve akıntı (leeway/set) gemiyi rot: Wind and current (leeway/set) push the ship off its course; even if the helmsman holds the heading on the compass, the ship may be set sideways. In pilotage and narrow waters, the OOW/pilot compensates for this using transits/leading lines and helm orders; the helmsman carries out the orders given exactly and reports any persistent offset noticed (e.g., "she's carrying port helm").
SOLAS Bölüm II-1 Kural 42-44'e göre tüm: Under SOLAS Chapter II-1 Regulations 42-44, all passenger ships and cargo ships of 500 GT and above must have an emergency source of power. The emergency generator must come on line automatically within 45 seconds of loss of main power.
SOLAS III/19, giriş veya kurtarma görevi: SOLAS III/19 requires enclosed space entry and rescue drills at least once every two months for personnel with entry or rescue duties. The Bosun ensures that the team drills realistic rescue scenarios, because in a real incident a correct and rapid rescue is only possible with a reflex built up through drills.
SOLAS III/19.3.3 gereği enclosed space e: Under SOLAS III/19.3.3, an enclosed space entry and rescue drill must be held at least once every 2 months; the planning and content of the drill are based on III/19.3.6 and the recommendations of IMO Res. A.1203(33). Enclosed space accidents are usually multiplied by the deaths of the "second person rushing to the rescue"; this is why the attendant never goes in, but raises the alarm and waits for the equipped rescue team.
SOLAS III/20.6 ve III/20.7 gereği filika: Under SOLAS III/20.6 and III/20.7, lifeboats are subject to a weekly visual inspection and engine run and to a monthly detailed inspection. In the weekly inspection, the lifeboat and launching appliance are inspected visually, and the engine is run for a total of at least 3 minutes. In the monthly inspection, the completeness of the inventory, running of the engine for at least 3 minutes, and the condition of the davit and falls are checked.
SOLAS V/34, geminin sefere çıkmadan önce: SOLAS V/34 clearly states that, before the ship proceeds to sea, the Master must ensure that the intended voyage has been planned (passage plan) using the appropriate charts and nautical publications. The plan must be prepared on a berth-to-berth basis; route selection, adequate depth, expected weather and currents, traffic density, anchorages, abort points and contingency anchorages must be included as integral parts of the plan. It is not enough for the Master simply to "sign" the plan; the Master is expected to actually review whether the plan is suitable for the ship type, the nature of the voyage and the competence of the crew.
SOLAS VI/5.6 ve VII, konteynerler dahil: SOLAS VI/5.6 and VII require all cargo units, including containers, to be stowed and secured in accordance with a ship-specific Cargo Securing Manual approved by the Administration/class. The CSM contains the ship's lashing equipment inventory, the MSL (Maximum Securing Load) of each item, approved lashing patterns, securing device arrangement plans and calculation methods. MSC.1/Circ.1353 is the guideline for its preparation.
SOLAS gemilerinde en az üç (300 GT ve üz: SOLAS ships carry at least three (at least two on cargo ships of 300 GT and upwards but less than 500 GT) waterproof portable VHF radios (survival craft two-way VHF). These are for on-scene communication from survival craft. The primary battery is sealed and for emergency use only; a separate rechargeable battery is for routine/test use.
SOLAS, belirli drill'leri zorunlu frekan: SOLAS requires certain drills to be carried out at mandatory intervals: abandon ship and fire drills every month (SOLAS III/19.3.2); every week on passenger ships (SOLAS III/30.2). Personnel joining the ship are given training in the life-saving and fire-fighting appliances within two weeks at the latest (SOLAS III/19.4.1). An enclosed space entry/rescue drill is carried out at least every 2 months, lifeboat launching and maneuvering in the water at least every 3 months, and rescue boat launching monthly as far as practicable and in any case at least every 3 months (SOLAS III/19.3). The Master plans this schedule and ensures that drills are carried out realistically and not just "on paper".
SOLAS, çeşitli tatbikatları zorunlu kıla: SOLAS makes various drills mandatory: abandon ship and fire drills (every month; and within 24 hours of leaving port if more than 25% of the crew have not taken part in drills on board that ship in the previous month), enclosed space rescue (every two months), steering gear test; pollution/SOPEP drills are required by the SOPEP and the SMS. The Safety Officer keeps the drill schedule, varies the scenarios and makes them realistic.
SOPEP, sahil otoritesi irtibat listesini: The SOPEP contains the list of coastal State contacts and the company's emergency contacts; this list must be kept up to date. On tankers certified to carry NLS (chemical tankers), a combined SMPEP (covering Annex I + II) may be carried instead of the SOPEP.
SOx uyumu BDN kükürt içeriği veya scrubb: SOx compliance is demonstrated by the BDN sulfur content or by the scrubber's exhaust SO₂/CO₂ ratio monitoring data; for NOx, the engines are set in accordance with the Technical File. In ECAs, the stricter limits are applied.
SSSCL, \"ben doldurdum\" değil \"birlikt: The SSSCL works on the principle of "we verified it together", not "I filled it in". Every item is physically checked and marked with the codes A (agreement), P (permission) and R (re-check).
STCW 2010 Manila değişiklikleri, vardiya: The STCW 2010 Manila amendments explicitly require watchkeeping personnel to be "fit for duty". Section A-VIII/1 requires Administrations to establish an alcohol limit of not more than 0.05% (0.5 g/L) blood alcohol concentration (BAC) or 0.25 mg/L alcohol in the breath. Many commercial operators tighten this further, applying 0.04% (OCIMF upper limit) or 0.00% on board.
STCW A-VIII/2, gündüz ve uygun koşullard: STCW A-VIII/2 may permit the officer to keep watch as the sole lookout in daylight and in suitable conditions; however, this applies only after the situation has been fully assessed and provided that assistance is immediately available to be summoned to the bridge when needed. When visibility decreases, as night approaches, in heavy traffic or whenever any doubt arises, the officer must immediately call for an additional lookout.
STCW Manila değişiklikleri, ECDIS'i prim: The Manila amendments to STCW require officers on ships using ECDIS as the primary means of navigation to have completed generic ECDIS training (IMO Model Course 1.27); in addition, the ISM Code (6.3) and STCW Regulation I/14 require type-specific familiarization with the particular ECDIS model on board. The Second Officer verifies that an officer newly joining the ship has completed both and personally carries out the type-specific familiarization.
Safety Officer, bu servislerin geçerlili: The Safety Officer tracks the validity dates of these services and plans them to fit the survey window. The service report (certificate) is kept on board; PSC and class surveyors ask for these certificates. For free-fall lifeboats, a free-fall launch or the simulated launching alternative (MSC.1/Circ.1206) is carried out at intervals of not more than 6 months.
Safety Officer, personel değişiminde mus: The Safety Officer updates the muster list immediately at a crew change; the duty of a person who leaves must not remain unassigned. Every new crew member learns their muster station, the location of their lifejacket and their escape route through familiarization before being assigned shipboard duties; on-board training in the ship's life-saving and firefighting appliances is given within 2 weeks at the latest.
Safety Officer, yolcu gemilerinde yolcul: On passenger ships, the Safety Officer also coordinates the muster procedure for passengers (on voyages where passengers are scheduled to be on board for more than 24 hours, a muster of newly embarked passengers prior to or immediately upon departure). On cargo ships, the focus is crew familiarization; the checklist is signed and kept as the familiarization record.
Sample 4 şişeye paylaştırılır: gemide sa: The sample is divided into 4 bottles: one retained on board as the ship's sample, one sent to a laboratory such as FOBAS/VPS, a supplier copy and the MARPOL sample (kept on board for at least 12 months for PSC). Until the lab report arrives (CCAI, density, viscosity, water content, sulfur, vanadium, aluminum + silicon, sediment; ignition risk if CCAI > 870), the fuel is not used; if it is urgently needed, its use at risk despite the quality doubt is recorded.
Scavenge fire tespitinde yük derhal düşü: When a scavenge fire is detected, the load is reduced immediately, fuel to the cylinder concerned is cut off, the scavenge drains are closed and the fixed smothering system (CO2/steam) is kept ready. Extra care is needed so that the fire does not lead to a crankcase explosion through the connection with the crankcase (piston rod stuffing box).
Sea valve / overboard valve gibi su altı: Underwater valves such as sea valves/overboard valves are regarded as "critical"; their opening/closing tests and tightness are carefully recorded. If the work is below the ship's waterline, it may require divers or dry-dock conditions.
Separatör overhaul'da bowl, conta ve O-r: In a separator overhaul, the bowl, gasket and O-ring sets are renewed; the bowl assembly sequence and balance are critical (incorrect assembly causes vibration and accidents). Loss of the water seal (broken water seal) causes fuel to escape through the water outlet to the sludge tank, while poor separation lets water/solids reach the main engine. The Second Engineer monitors separator vibration and leakage daily.
Separatörde water seal (su contası) doğr: If the water seal in the separator is not established correctly, fuel/oil escapes through the water outlet (oil loss) or water passes to the fuel side. The Oiler checks that the sludge discharge has the correct color (dark sludge) and that no clean fuel/oil is being lost, and reports any deviation to the engineer.
Sert plastik konteyner (canister) veya y: Packed in a rigid plastic container (canister) or in a soft valise: CO₂/N₂ cylinder, buoyancy tubes + canopy, painter line.
Side-rolling tip: panel raylar üzerinde: Side-rolling type: the panels roll sideways on rails; suitable for large hatch openings, common on bulk carriers.
Silindir yağı, gömleğe ölçülü dozlarla (: Cylinder oil is fed to the liner in metered doses (cylinder lubricators / Alpha lubrication); the base number (BN) of the oil is selected according to the fuel sulfur content in order to neutralize the sulfur in the fuel. Under MARPOL Annex VI, EGR or SCR is used for NOx in the NOx ECAs where Tier III applies, and low-sulfur fuel or a scrubber is used to meet the SOx limits (0.50% globally, 0.10% in SECAs).
Sintine kuyusu, çift dip tank, kofferdam: Bilge wells, double bottom tanks, cofferdams, sludge tanks, boilers and similar enclosed spaces may be deficient in oxygen or accumulate toxic gases (H₂S, CO) and flammable gas. These spaces are entered only after the atmosphere has been tested with a calibrated instrument and an entry permit has been issued.
SoF'tan türetilen time sheet, laytime'ın: The time sheet derived from the SoF shows how laytime was used up: which periods counted as laytime and which were excluded as exceptions (excepted periods — e.g. weather, equipment breakdown). The Chief Officer makes sure that stoppages that should count as laytime (caused by the charterer/terminal) are recorded correctly; this protects demurrage income.
Sonuçlar BDN ve ISO 8217 limitleriyle ka: The results are compared with the BDN and the ISO 8217 limits. If a result exceeds a MARPOL limit (e.g. sulfur), the flag State is notified; other off-spec results are handled as a commercial claim with the supplier.
Spektrometrik analiz (ASTM D5185/D6595),: Spectrometric analysis (ASTM D5185/D6595) measures metals at ppm level. Fe indicates ring/liner/crank wear; copper (Cu), bearings/cooler tubes; chromium (Cr), rings/valves; aluminum (Al), pistons/bearings; lead-tin (Pb/Sn), wear of bearing surfaces.
Spring line: Gemiden rıhtıma boylamasına: Spring line: a line leading from the ship to the quay in a fore-and-aft direction. The fore spring (leading aft from forward) prevents the ship from moving ahead, and the aft spring (leading forward from aft) prevents it from moving astern.
Stajyer, COLREG'in en çok uygulanan kura: The cadet observes the most frequently applied COLREG rules in real encounters and learns that in a head-on situation (Rule 14) both ships must alter course to starboard, and which ship is the "stand-on" ship (not the one that gives way, but the one that keeps her course) and which is the "give-way" ship in crossing (Rule 15) and overtaking (Rule 13) situations. The cadet sees in practice why the principle that action must be early, readily apparent and sufficient (Rule 8) matters: small and late maneuvers may not be noticed by the other ship.
Stajyer, gece köprüüstü vardiyalarında d: During night bridge watches, the cadet learns to determine the type, size and aspect (angle of approach) of other ships by reading their lights (Part C): sidelights (red port, green starboard), forward/aft masthead lights, towing/pushing lights, and the special lights of fishing vessels, pilot vessels and vessels restricted in their ability to maneuver. Day shapes (ball, cone, cylinder, diamond) and sound signals in restricted visibility and maneuvering signals are also learned in practice.
Stajyer, giriş izni, sürekli haberleşme,: The cadet learns about the entry permit, continuous communication, rescue equipment (resuscitator, EEBD, winch/tripod) and the role of the attendant. One of the most dangerous scenarios is that a second person, entering without precautions to rescue a colleague who has collapsed inside, also dies; the rescue plan is therefore prepared in advance.
Stajyer; FO settling/service tank, DO ta: The cadet learns to read the levels of the FO settling/service tanks, DO tank, LO sump, fresh water tanks, cooling water expansion tank and bilge holding tank both remotely (remote level gauge) and manually (sounding pipe + tape). Manual sounding is vital when the automatic level gauge fails or when verification is needed.
Stajyer; mooring winch (bağlama vinci),: The cadet learns the function of equipment such as the mooring winch, the anchor windlass, the vertical warping drum, warping drums, stoppers (mooring line/chain stoppers) and roller fairleads. How many turns of the line are to be taken on the drum, rendering (controlled slipping) and use of the brake are critical skills. The cadet observes the lubrication of the equipment, brake testing and the concept of rendered brake capacity.
Storage tank ısıtması, transfer öncesi p: Storage tank heating is to obtain a pumpable viscosity before transfer. Overheating (condensation/flashpoint risk) and local overheating inside the tank (water ingress through a coil leak) are avoided.
Sözleşme, büyük tanker kazalarının (Torr: The Convention was strengthened following major tanker accidents (Torrey Canyon 1967; the accidents of 1976-77).
Sınırlı görüş anında COLREG Rule 5, 19 v: In restricted visibility, special precautions come into effect under COLREG Rules 5, 19 and 35: safe speed, fog signals, engines ready, additional lookout. The Master is called to the bridge immediately. Radar/ARPA operation, target tracking quality (true vs relative motion), and the sea clutter and rain clutter settings must be under the Master's control.
T/C devri, scavenge air pressure ve egzo: T/C speed, scavenge air pressure and exhaust back pressure are written in the daily log. Compressor-side fouling (oily air filter, oil deposits) and turbine-side fouling (carbon deposits) lead to a loss of efficiency over time. A periodic cleaning procedure is applied (compressor side: wet wash; turbine side: dry (granule) wash or wet wash).
TMSA Element 4 (vessel reliability ve ma: Under TMSA Element 4 (vessel reliability and maintenance), planned purchasing, the use of frame agreements and cost control must be demonstrated. The Chief Engineer documents this competence through the requisition history and budget reports.
TMSA'nın engine room operations ve envir: The TMSA elements covering engine room operations and environmental management directly concern the engine department. The Chief Engineer meets the KPI and best practice requirements of these elements at ship level.
Tank içine giriş öncesi gas-freeing (hav: Before entry into a tank, gas-freeing (ventilation) brings the hydrocarbon and toxic gas levels to safe values and the oxygen to ~21%; the enclosed space entry procedure, gas measurement and permit are applied. Before an inerted tank is gas-freed with air, it is purged with inert gas until the hydrocarbon content is below 2% by volume, so that the tank atmosphere does not pass through the flammable range.
Tank top seviyesi ve sintine alanları da: The tank top level and the bilge areas can be cramped and hot; when working in these areas, the enclosed space rules are reviewed. Regular cleaning also slows down corrosion in these areas; accumulated salt water corrodes the steel. The Wiper tries to leave every point reached clean and dry.
Tank yıkama suyu ve tortu (slop), petrol: Because tank washings and sediment (slops) contain oil, they cannot be discharged into the sea unless the conditions of MARPOL Annex I Reg. 34 are met; MARPOL Annex I sets out the rules for reducing slops by COW, collecting them in the slop tank, separating oil and water, and appropriate discharge/delivery. The Oil Record Book is the legal document in which all washing, slop transfer and discharge operations are recorded. The AB assists with the physical work of these operations and prevents spills and leaks.
Tanker pump room ve kargo tankları, hidr: Tanker pump rooms and cargo tanks are high-risk with regard to hydrocarbon vapor and oxygen deficiency. In a tank filled with inert gas, the oxygen content does not exceed 8% by volume and the atmosphere cannot sustain life; entry is prohibited until a gas-free certificate has been obtained. ISGOTT defines additional procedures for enclosed space entry on tankers (gas-freeing, continuous monitoring). The Chief Officer ensures these conditions in coordination with the cargo officer.
Tankerlerde hot work, hazardous zone dış: On tankers, hot work is done outside the hazardous zone or under conditions where the work area is fully gas-free and adjacent cargo tanks are inerted or gas-freed. The Chief Officer verifies that there are no flammable sources within a 30 m radius of the work point, that the decks below, where sparks may fall, are protected, and that fire-fighting equipment is at hand.
Tarih boyunca denizcilerin yaşadığı skor: Scurvy, which seafarers suffered from throughout history, is the classic example of vitamin C deficiency; it shows itself through bleeding gums, weakness and delayed wound healing. The cook prevents it by protecting vitamin C sources (citrus fruit, sauerkraut, frozen vegetables, fruit juice concentrate) in the last weeks of a long voyage. Fe-deficiency anemia, vitamin D deficiency and B12 deficiency are also risks to watch for on long voyages.
Taze hava girişi: Minimum taze hava mikt: Fresh air intake: The minimum quantity of fresh air is supplied.
Hazards: CO₂ is lethal to humans. Before release, it must be verified that all personnel have been evacuated.
Tek bir okuma değil, zaman içindeki eğil: What matters is not a single reading but the trend over time. A slow rise in the exhaust temperature of one cylinder compared with the others points to a fuel valve/injector problem; a gradual rise in jacket cooling water temperature points to a fouled/clogged cooler or a thermostat problem; a slow fall in LO pressure points to a clogged filter or pump wear.
Tek bumbalı jib vinç: En yaygın gemi vin: Single-jib crane: the most common type of ship's crane. It may be electro-hydraulic or all-electric. It has hoisting, luffing and slewing motions.
Temizlik sonrası sintine kuru tutulur; b: After cleaning, the bilge is kept dry, so that any new leak becomes visible at once. A painted, clean bilge gives early warning to the crew as much as to the inspector.
Test sonuçları (start süresi, gerilim/fr: Test results (start time, voltage/frequency recovery, behavior on load) are recorded in the engine logbook and the PMS log. To assess cold-start capability, the ETO also tests the engine with the jacket water heater (jacket heater) on and off; the start time may be longer when the engine is cold.
Tide Tables (ATT) yıllık bir üründür; ge: The Admiralty Tide Tables (ATT) are an annual publication; the current year's edition must be carried, because tidal predictions are specific to each year. The Tidal Stream Atlases, The Mariner's Handbook (NP100), the Annual Summary of Admiralty Notices to Mariners and the relevant Catalogue of Admiralty Charts (NP131) are also kept up to date.
Title 4, denizcilerin karadaki refah ola: Title 4 supports seafarers' access to welfare facilities ashore (seamen's clubs, recreation, communication); shipowners and port States are encouraged to provide welfare facilities. In the modern era, internet/communication access on board (contact with family) has become a basic component of mental health. The Master supports reasonable use of the right to shore leave; preventing shore leave other than because of ISPS/operational restrictions is a welfare violation.
Toksik ve yanıcı olması nedeniyle özel g: Because it is toxic and flammable, it requires special safety precautions. Class rules require it to be located in a separate gastight compartment, apart from the engine room.
Traffic Separation Schemes (TSS), COLREG: Traffic Separation Schemes (TSS) are governed by COLREG Rule 10. The basic rules are that the ship proceeds in the general direction of traffic flow, avoids crossing traffic lanes as far as practicable (and, if obliged to cross, does so on a heading as nearly as practicable at right angles to the general direction of traffic flow), and does not use the inshore traffic zone between the coast and the TSS when she can safely use the adjacent traffic lane (except vessels of less than 20 m, sailing vessels, vessels engaged in fishing, vessels en route to or from a place within the zone, or to avoid immediate danger). In busy TSSs such as Dover, Ouessant and the Bosphorus, the Master takes the conn personally.
Transfer öncesi scupper'lar tıkanır (plu: Before transfer, the scuppers are plugged and drip trays are put in place; any spill on deck is prevented from reaching the sea. No transfer is carried out until the plugs are fitted.
Tüm sistemler, İdare (Administration) ta: All systems must be type-approved by the Administration in accordance with the IMO requirements (G8 / BWMS Code); systems that use active substances also require approval by IMO.
UMS modunda dahi günde en az bir kez (ge: Even in UMS mode, a detailed engine room round is made at least once a day (usually in the morning). The dead man alarm system raises an alarm if a person working alone in the engine room does not reset it at set intervals; this saves lives in the event of unconsciousness or an accident.
UTC; GNSS alıcılarından, radyo zaman sin: UTC is obtained from GNSS receivers, radio time signals (listed in ALRS Vol. 2) and internet time services. Although GPS is the primary source, the Second Officer keeps up the habit of cross-checking with a backup source; dependence on a single source puts time integrity at risk if that source fails.
Uluslararası Tarih Hattı (IDL), yaklaşık: The International Date Line (IDL) roughly follows the 180° meridian and is the date boundary between the eastern and western hemispheres. The time differences that build up going east and west from Greenwich reach exactly 24 hours at 180°; for this reason the date is changed by one day when the line is crossed. When crossing from west to east (sailing eastbound, W to E), the date is put back one day (the same date is lived twice); when crossing from east to west (sailing westbound, E to W), the date is advanced one day (a day is skipped).
Uzun bakım vardiyaları, gece çalışmaları: Long periods of maintenance work, night work and busy port stays increase fatigue. Most human-factor accidents arise from the four factors of "haste, carelessness, habit blindness and fatigue". Safety culture is the discipline of "doing it right and safely" in the face of pressure to "finish quickly".
Uzun okyanus geçişlerinde taze meyve/seb: On long ocean passages, the intake of vitamin C and other micronutrients falls as fresh fruit/vegetables run out; this is why seafarers historically suffered from scurvy. As fresh produce runs out, the cook conserves the sources of vitamin C: citrus juices, sauerkraut, frozen vegetables and, when necessary, supplements/fruit juice concentrate are brought into use. Red meat, pulses, dairy products and whole grains are kept on the menu as sources of minerals (Fe, calcium) and B-group vitamins.
V/34-1 maddesi ise kaptanın seyir emniye: Regulation V/34-1 clearly provides that the Master's decisions on safe navigation are based on "professional judgement" and that no company, charterer or third party may act in a way that prevents such decisions. In practice, this provision is referred to as "overriding authority", which is also emphasized in ISM Code section 5.2. ISM internal audits look for concrete evidence that the company does not obstruct the Master's exercise of this authority.
VSAT kesildiğinde, gemi alternatif bağla: When the VSAT link is lost, the ship switches to an alternative link: Inmarsat FleetBroadband (L-band, resistant to rain fade but low speed), GSM/4G in port and MF/HF in an emergency. The ETO manages the automatic failover (least-cost routing) configuration and knows the manual changeover procedure; keeping critical operational traffic uninterrupted is the priority.
Wages account, allotment kayıtları ve re: Wage statements, allotment records and rest hour records are also kept under the MLC. Common MLC findings at PSC include missing SEAs, inconsistencies in wage records and rest hour violations.
Windlass kapasitesi Equipment Number (EN: Windlass capacity is determined by the Equipment Number (EN). The EN value depends on the ship's displacement, breadth, effective height from the summer load waterline to the top of the uppermost deckhouse, and lateral (profile) area.
Yakıt (FO) ve yağlama yağı (LO) purifier: Fuel oil (FO) and lubricating oil (LO) purifiers are high-speed centrifugal separators (e.g. Alfa Laval, Westfalia/GEA) used to remove water/sludge. During periodic maintenance, the bowl is dismantled, the disc stack is cleaned of sludge, and the main seal ring and operating water valves are checked. The gravity disc is selected according to the fuel density; a wrong gravity disc shifts the oil/water interface: a disc with too large a hole breaks the water seal so that oil escapes through the water outlet, while one with too small a hole impairs separation and lets water into the cleaned oil.
Yakıt operasyonlarında yanıcı buhar biri: Flammable vapor can accumulate during fuel operations. Throughout bunkering, the ban on naked flames/smoking is enforced, no hot work is done and ventilation is provided. Suitable fire extinguishers are kept ready around the manifold.
Yakıt/yağ ROB değerleri, günlük tüketim: Fuel/oil ROB figures, daily consumption and bunkers received are recorded regularly. Under MARPOL Annex VI, the Bunker Delivery Note (BDN) and the sample are retained; the accuracy of consumption data has become increasingly critical for IMO DCS/CII reporting.
Yangın hattı (fire main) hidrantları ve: The fire main supplies the hydrants and the fixed extinguishing systems; through the ISC (international shore connection), water can be supplied to the fire main from shore or from another ship.
Yardımcı dizel motor genellikle dört zam: The auxiliary diesel engine is usually of the four-stroke, medium-speed type. It generates electricity running at 720 or 900 rpm for 60 Hz, or at 750 or 1000 rpm for 50 Hz.
Yağ veya solvent bulaşmış bezler (örneği: Cloths contaminated with oil or solvent (e.g. oily rags from the engine room) are NEVER put in the dryer; they can ignite at dryer temperatures (spontaneous combustion). No combustible material is placed next to a running dryer, and the machine is not left running unattended for long periods. Checks are made that the laundry fire detector and the fire damper are in working order, that the detector is not covered and that the damper flap is kept open.
Yağcı, ECA geçişinde filtre DP'sini ve y: During the ECA changeover, the Oiler closely monitors filter DP and fuel temperature; a sudden change in viscosity can cause seal leaks or pump cavitation. The changeover is carried out gradually, and the time and position are recorded in the fuel changeover logbook.
Yağcı, bunker yoğunluğuna göre üretici t: The Oiler selects the correct disc from the manufacturer's table (gravity disc selection chart) according to the bunker density. When the densities of modern HFOs approach 991 kg/m³ (at 15°C), water separation in a conventional purifier becomes difficult; for this reason, new-generation separators (systems such as ALCAP) control the interface automatically without a gravity disc.
Yağcı, kapalı alanda çalışırken zaman sı: When working in an enclosed space, the Oiler knows the time limit, the escape route and the communication signals. When the gas alarm sounds or if they feel unwell, the Oiler gets out immediately, without hesitation. The enclosed space entry and rescue drills held at least every two months under SOLAS III/19 keep these skills alive.
Yağcı, muster list'te boundary cooling g: If the Oiler is assigned to boundary cooling in the muster list, they cool the decks/bulkheads adjacent to the fire compartment with a hose; water evaporating shows that the surface is still overheated and cooling must continue. Excessive use of water is avoided so that accumulated water (free surface) does not impair stability and so that drainage remains open.
Yağcı, numune şişelerinin temiz olmasına: The Oiler helps ensure that the sample bottles are clean, correctly labeled and sealed. The sample is evidence of the fuel quality (ISO 8217 compliance, sulfur content); in an off-spec fuel claim, this sample is decisive.
Yük operasyonunda dökülen tahıl, toz, hi: Grain, dust, hydraulic oil or chemicals spilled during cargo operations are both a safety and an environmental risk. Under MARPOL, discharging cargo residues or chemical spills into the sea is prohibited in port and within 12 NM of land; residues accumulating on deck are not swept overboard but collected.
